title: Random forest diagnoses peripheral arterial disease in people over 80
summary: In 539 participants over 80 years old, a random forest model had sensitivity 89.3% and specificity 91.6%, compared with 81.5%/83.8% for logistic regression and 85.1%/84.5% for the ankle-brachial index. A seven-feature random forest tested in a prospective study reached 100.0% sensitivity and 90.3% specificity. The prospective sample is small.
ai_technology: Random forest on routine clinical and blood features

evidence.tested: Retrospective model comparison in 539 participants and a prospective study of a reduced seven-feature model.
evidence.unknown: Prospective cohort size not stated in the abstract; elderly cohort only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest diagnoses PAD from routine features.
